title: The rikma's API
subtitle: Connect an outside system — a ticket desk, a bug board, a contact form, a bot — and every item it opens opens here too, as a task in the rikma.
consentNote: A task created through the API is an offer, not an assignment: it is registered under someone's name only after they accept it here in the platform. A leaked key can propose work — it cannot commit anyone to it.
noKeys: No active key for this rikma yet.
scope_tasks_read: Check what happened to a task it opened
revokeConfirm: Revoke this key? Every system using it stops working immediately.
saveWarning: Save the key now — it is shown once and cannot be recovered.
secretLabel: The webhook signing secret — also shown only once:
idsSubtitle: These are the numbers your external system has to quote. Click an id to copy it.
noMissions: No missions are in progress in this rikma right now.
noRoles: No roles are defined on this rikma's missions.
name: Name
createKeyFirst: Create a key so the code is generated with the real key instead of a placeholder.
serverHint: Call this from your server, not from the browser: a key sent to the browser is visible to anyone who views the page source.
varName: The task's name as it will appear in the rikma
varExternalId: Your own id for the item. Sending it again never opens a second task.
varDescLink: Full description and a link back to the original item
varMissionId: The in-progress mission this task hangs on
varAssignedUserId: The member the task is offered to
varRoleIds: The role the task is offered to — instead of a specific member
varUrgency: red / yellow / green / white. Defaults to white
varDates: Start and end dates, ISO format
varsNote: Send assignedUserId or roleIds — never both. The rikma itself is derived from the key and is never sent from outside, which is what stops one rikma's key from reaching another.
agentSubtitle: Paste this into the agent building your site — it carries the whole contract plus the ids you picked above.
